# quality


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A search engine ranks pages by how well they match a query. That is not
the same as how worth reading they are. A question about building rules
in Australia can return five cost guides from one trade directory ahead
of the government page that sets the rules. A programming question can
return sites that copy Stack Overflow answers.

This module reorders results before any page is downloaded. It does
these things:

- It removes copycat sites.
- It moves sources that have authority on the kind of question up the
  list.
- It limits how many results one website can have near the top.
- It splits a question that asks several things into one search per
  part.

[`research`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#research) in
`fossick.search` calls
[`curate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#curate)
when `curated=True`, its default. It also uses
[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#plan) and
[`interleave`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#interleave).
Each function here also works on its own, on any list of result
dictionaries with an `href` or `url`.

## Which site a URL belongs to

Two URLs belong to the same site when they share a registrable domain,
the part of the name someone registered: `docs.python.org` and
`www.python.org` both belong to `python.org`. Usually that is the last
two parts of the host name. In countries whose registries sell names one
level down, such as `bbc.co.uk` or `nsw.gov.au`, it is the last three.
`MULTI_LABEL_SUFFIXES` lists those registry endings for the countries
fossick handles.
[`host`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#host)
returns a URL’s host name in lower case without `www.`, and
[`registrable_domain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#registrable_domain)
returns the site.

## One key per page

The same page often appears under several URLs: with and without `www.`,
with a trailing slash, or with tracking parameters such as `utm_source`
added by whoever shared it.
[`norm_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#norm_url)
reduces a URL to one key. It drops the scheme, the `www.`, the fragment,
tracking parameters, a default port and a trailing slash. It sorts the
query parameters. A port that is not the default stays in the key.
[`interleave`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#interleave),
[`cluster_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#cluster_sources)
and
[`diversity`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#diversity)
use the key to decide when two results are the same page.

## Authority depends on the question

The source to trust depends on the question. For a question about the
law, a government site is the authority. For a question about a library,
its documentation is. For a question about what users think, a forum is.
`DOMAIN_RULES` lists, for each kind of question, the sites to move up
(`boost`) and the sites to move down (`demote`). The kinds are `docs`,
`policy`, `release`, `security` and `community`.

[`domain_matches`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#domain_matches)
checks one host name against one rule. A rule has one of four forms:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Rule</th>
<th>Matches</th>
<th>Example</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Ends in a dot</td>
<td>Host names that start with it</td>
<td><code>docs.</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Starts with a dot</td>
<td>The ending itself and every host under it</td>
<td><code>.gov.au</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Contains a <code>/</code></td>
<td>Only the host name before the <code>/</code>, with no
subdomains</td>
<td><code>github.com/advisories</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Any other text</td>
<td>That domain and its subdomains</td>
<td><code>sec.gov</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Only a rule that ends in a dot matches the start of a host name.
`openai.com.evil.example` does not match `openai.com`.
[`blocked_matches`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#blocked_matches)
applies the last form, the domain and its subdomains, to a blocked list.

## What kind of question it is

[`classify`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#classify)
reads the kind of question from the cue words in `INTENT_CUES`.
“regulation” and “permit” indicate `policy`. “release notes” indicates
`release`.
[`classify`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#classify)
returns the kind with the most cue matches. It returns None when the
query has no cues or when two kinds tie. With None,
[`curate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#curate)
does not reorder the results by authority.

## Copycat sites and `site:`

`SPAM_MIRRORS` lists sites that copy the content of other sites, such as
Stack Overflow scrapers and GitHub mirrors. They add nothing to the
original. Searching several engines tends to promote them, because they
are built to rank on all of them.

[`drop_spam`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#drop_spam)
removes results from these sites and from any extra domains in
`blocked`. It returns the remaining results and the domains removed. A
domain in `allowed` is kept even when it is on a list. `allowed` also
covers the subdomains of that domain.

A query that contains `site:reddit.com` has already chosen its site.
[`site_domains`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#site_domains)
returns the domains named by `site:` in a query. For such a query,
[`curate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#curate)
skips the copycat removal and the per-site limit, which would undo the
choice.
[`curate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#curate)
still reorders by authority.

## Splitting a question into searches

A question such as “I want to rebuild my garage in australia, cheap
options, what is the regulation on it, material options” asks three
things. One search for all of it mostly finds pages about the first.
[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#plan) splits
it into one search per part.

[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#plan)
removes openings such as “I want to” (`LEAD_INS`) and empty phrases
(`FILLER`). It splits the rest at commas, semicolons, question marks and
words such as “and”. It adds the topic words of the first part to each
later part. Each search then still says “garage australia”. The original
question is always the first search.

[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#plan)
returns `[q]` when there is nothing to split. The table lists the
conditions.

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Condition</th>
<th>Result</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>max_queries</code> is below 2</td>
<td><code>[q]</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The query has fewer than <code>min_words</code> words</td>
<td><code>[q]</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The query has <code>site:</code></td>
<td><code>[q]</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The query has only one part</td>
<td><code>[q]</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The later parts add no new words to the first</td>
<td><code>[q]</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`max_queries` caps the number of searches. `rewrite` is a function, such
as a call to a language model, that takes the question and returns a
list of searches. When you pass it,
[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#plan) uses
it instead of these rules.
[`facets`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#facets)
returns the parts as lists of topic words.

[`interleave`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#interleave)
merges the result lists of several searches. It takes one result from
each list in turn and keeps a page that several searches found once. For
such a page it joins the `queries` lists of the duplicate results.
Taking turns gives each part of the question its own sources. Merging by
score would favour the general guide that ranks for every part over the
specific source that answers one part.

## Reordering

[`authority_rerank`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#authority_rerank)
moves results from the sites that `DOMAIN_RULES` boosts for a kind of
question to the front. It moves results from the sites that
`DOMAIN_RULES` demotes towards the back.
[`cap_per_domain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#cap_per_domain)
lets each site keep at most `max_per` results near the top and moves the
rest to the end of the list in their original order. A list of fewer
than three results is returned unchanged.

Neither function drops a result. Results that are not moved keep their
order. Both return the reordered list and a second value. For
[`authority_rerank`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#authority_rerank)
it is a report dictionary with `intent`, `applied`, `boosted` and
`demoted`. For
[`cap_per_domain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#cap_per_domain)
it is the number of results moved to the end.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## How many stories, not how many URLs

Ten results can be one story, for example a news agency report that nine
sites reprinted.
[`cluster_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#cluster_sources)
groups results that have the same
[`norm_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#norm_url)
key or that share most of their text.

[`shingles`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#shingles)
returns the set of three-word sequences in a text.
[`jaccard`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#jaccard)
divides the size of the overlap of two sets by the size of their union.
[`cluster_sources`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#cluster_sources)
applies
[`jaccard`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#jaccard)
to the shingles of each result’s title and text. Two results with a
similarity at or above `threshold` (0.6 by default) are one story. The
grouping is transitive. When A matches B and B matches C, all three are
one group. Each group is named after its first member in the input
order.

[`independence`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#independence)
returns the groups with a score. The score rises with the number of
separate stories and the number of separate sites. The result also lists
its limits. Two sites that rewrite one press release in their own words
do not share enough text to be grouped.

## Describing a result list

[`diversity`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#diversity)
describes a list and does not change it. The result has these keys:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>n</code>, <code>domains</code></td>
<td>Number of results and number of sites</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>dominant_domain</code></td>
<td>The site with the most results, and its <code>share</code> of the
results</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>dup_urls</code></td>
<td>Number of results whose <a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#norm_url"><code>norm_url</code></a>
key repeats an earlier one</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>near_dups</code></td>
<td>Number of pairs of results that read alike</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>sources</code></td>
<td>Number of separate stories</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>score</code></td>
<td>A number from 0 to 1. A higher number means a more varied list.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The `score` is the weighted sum of three components.

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Component</th>
<th>Weight</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Share of separate sites</td>
<td>0.5</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Share of unique URLs</td>
<td>0.3</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Share of pairs that do not read alike</td>
<td>0.2</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

[`snippet_similarity`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#snippet_similarity)
returns the Jaccard similarity of the three-word sequences of two texts.

## [`curate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#curate)

[`curate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#curate)
runs these steps in order:

1.  [`drop_spam`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#drop_spam)
    removes copycat sites.
2.  [`authority_rerank`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#authority_rerank)
    reorders by authority for the kind of question.
    [`classify`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#classify)
    reads the kind from the query, or you pass `intent`. `intent=None`
    skips this step.
3.  [`cap_per_domain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#cap_per_domain)
    applies the per-site limit. `max_per_domain=0` skips this step.
4.  [`diversity`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#diversity)
    describes the result.

A query with `site:` skips steps 1 and 3.
[`curate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#curate)
returns the reordered results and a report of what each step did. With
`rerank=False` it returns the results untouched. The report then has
`dropped=[]`, `demoted=0` and `authority=None`, and still has `intent`
and
[`diversity`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#diversity).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/quality.py#L417"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### curate

``` python
def curate(
    q:str, # the query, read for intent and `site:` constraints
    hits:list, # search hits (dicts with `href`/`url`, `title`, `body`)
    intent:str='auto', # an intent class, 'auto' to classify, or None to skip authority
    max_per_domain:int=2, # per-registrable-domain cap; 0 disables
    blocked:tuple=(), allowed:tuple=(), # extra mirror domains, and rescues from the built-in list
    rerank:bool=True, # False: describe only, return `hits` untouched
)->tuple:
```

*Remove copycat sites, reorder by authority, limit results per site, and
return the results with a report.*

## Tests

The cells below test each function offline, mostly on the garage
question, which is the case this module was written for.

``` python
# registrable domain: the site behind a url, with the three-label registries handled
assert registrable_domain('https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html') == 'python.org'
assert registrable_domain('https://www.bbc.co.uk/news') == 'bbc.co.uk'
assert registrable_domain('https://planning.nsw.gov.au/x') == 'nsw.gov.au'
assert registrable_domain('https://wko.at/') == 'wko.at'
assert registrable_domain('https://x.com') == 'x.com' and registrable_domain('') == ''
assert registrable_domain('http://192.168.1.1/a') == '192.168.1.1'      # an ip has nothing to strip
assert host('https://WWW.Example.COM./p') == 'example.com'
```

``` python
# norm_url: one page has one key, and query order does not change the key
assert norm_url('https://www.x.com/a/?utm_source=t#frag') == norm_url('http://x.com/a')
assert norm_url('https://x.com/a') != norm_url('https://x.com/b')
assert norm_url('https://x.com/a?b=2&a=1') == norm_url('https://x.com/a?a=1&b=2')   # sorted
assert norm_url('https://x.com:443/a') == norm_url('https://x.com/a')               # default port
assert norm_url('https://x.com:8443/a') != norm_url('https://x.com/a')              # but not any port
assert norm_url('https://x.com/a?mkt_tok=z&_ga=1&keep=2') == norm_url('https://x.com/a?keep=2')
```

``` python
# rule matching is the security boundary, not just the ranking one
assert domain_matches('docs.python.org', 'docs.') and not domain_matches('notdocs.com', 'docs.')
assert domain_matches('planning.nsw.gov.au', '.gov.au')          # suffix rules cover a whole registry
assert domain_matches('gov.uk', '.gov.uk')                       # ...including the registry itself
assert domain_matches('abcb.gov.au', '.gov.au')
assert not domain_matches('hipages.com.au', '.gov.au')
assert domain_matches('sec.gov', 'sec.gov') and domain_matches('www.sec.gov', 'sec.gov')
assert not domain_matches('openai.com.evil.example', 'openai.com')   # never a bare startswith
assert blocked_matches('de.newbedev.com', 'newbedev.com')
assert not blocked_matches('newbedev.com.evil.example', 'newbedev.com')
```

``` python
# spam mirrors are removed; an explicit site: constraint skips the copycat removal and the per-site limit
_h = [dict(href='https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1', title='real'),
      dict(href='https://newbedev.com/questions/1', title='mirror'),
      dict(href='https://de.newbedev.com/q/1', title='mirror subdomain')]
_kept, _rm = drop_spam(_h)

assert drop_spam(_h, allowed=['newbedev.com'])[0] == _h            # allow rescues the subdomain too

assert site_domains('site:reddit.com/r/LocalLLaMA best server') == ['reddit.com']

_, _r = curate('site:reddit.com best local llm', [dict(href=f'https://reddit.com/{i}') for i in range(5)])
assert _r['site_constrained'] == ['reddit.com'] and _r['demoted'] == 0   # not diversified away
```

``` python
# authority: the garage query, which is what this is all for
_garage = [dict(href='https://hipages.com.au/article/garage-cost', title='How much to build a garage'),
           dict(href='https://oneflare.com.au/costs/garage', title='Garage costs 2026'),

assert _rep['authority']['applied'] and _rep['authority']['top_before'] == 'hipages.com.au'

# reranking drops nothing

# an unknown or absent intent is a no-op, not an error
assert authority_rerank(_garage, None)[0] == _garage
assert authority_rerank(_garage, 'nonsense')[1]['applied'] is False
```

``` python
# capping and diversity describe the five-listicles-from-one-site failure
_mono = [dict(href=f'https://hipages.com.au/a/{i}', title='Garage cost guide', body='what a garage costs')
         for i in range(5)] + [dict(href='https://abcb.gov.au/ncc', title='NCC', body='construction code')]
_capped, _n = cap_per_domain(_mono, 2)
assert _n == 3 and [host(_url(h)) for h in _capped][:3] == ['hipages.com.au']*2 + ['abcb.gov.au']
assert len(_capped) == len(_mono)                                    # moved, never dropped

_d = diversity(_mono)
assert _d['n'] == 6 and _d['domains'] == 2
assert _d['dominant_domain'] == dict(domain='hipages.com.au', share=round(5/6, 4))
assert _d['near_dups'] > 0                                           # the five guides read alike
assert diversity([])['n'] == 0 and diversity([])['score'] == 0.0

# a genuinely diverse set scores higher than a monopolised one
_div = [dict(href=f'https://s{i}.com/a', title=f'topic {i}', body=f'quite different text number {i}')
        for i in range(6)]
assert diversity(_div)['score'] > _d['score']
assert snippet_similarity('one two three four', 'one two three four') == 1.0
assert snippet_similarity('too short', 'too short') == 0.0           # no trigram evidence -> not a match
```

``` python
# planning: one question containing three
_GARAGE = ('I want to rebuild my garage in australia, cheap options, '
           'what is the regulation on it, material options')
_p = plan(_GARAGE)
assert _p[0] == _GARAGE                                   # the baseline is never given up
assert len(_p) == 4                                       # all three facets, plus the original
assert any('regulation' in s for s in _p[1:]), _p
assert any('cheap' in s for s in _p[1:]) and any('material' in s for s in _p[1:]), _p
assert all('garage' in s and 'australia' in s for s in _p[1:]), _p   # subject re-attached to each facet
assert 'want' not in _p[1] and 'what' not in _p[1]        # lead-in and filler stripped

# ...and constant abstention, which is what makes it safe to leave on
assert plan('sqlite wal mode vs journal mode performance') == ['sqlite wal mode vs journal mode performance']
assert plan('garage cost') == ['garage cost']                        # too short to hold two questions
assert plan('site:reddit.com best local llm, cheap options') == ['site:reddit.com best local llm, cheap options']
assert plan(_GARAGE, max_queries=1) == [_GARAGE]                     # explicitly disabled
assert plan('') == []
assert len(plan(_GARAGE, max_queries=2)) == 2                        # the cap is honoured

# a facet that adds no words to the subject is not a search
assert plan('rebuild my garage in australia, the garage, australia') == \
       ['rebuild my garage in australia, the garage, australia']

# an injected rewriter (a model, in ramabana) replaces the heuristic and still keeps the original
assert plan('anything at all here', rewrite=lambda q: ['one', 'two']) == ['anything at all here', 'one', 'two']
```

``` python
# interleaving is coverage, not consensus: the generalist that ranks for every facet must not
# outrank the specialist that owns one
_cost = [dict(href='https://hipages.com.au/guide', title='complete garage guide'),
         dict(href='https://oneflare.com.au/cost', title='costs')]
_reg  = [dict(href='https://hipages.com.au/guide', title='complete garage guide'),
         dict(href='https://planning.nsw.gov.au/exempt', title='exempt development')]
_mat  = [dict(href='https://hipages.com.au/guide', title='complete garage guide'),
         dict(href='https://bunnings.com.au/materials', title='materials')]
_il = interleave([_cost, _reg, _mat])
assert [host(_url(h)) for h in _il][:2] == ['hipages.com.au', 'oneflare.com.au']
assert 'planning.nsw.gov.au' in [host(_url(h)) for h in _il[:4]], [_url(h) for h in _il]
assert len(_il) == 4                                      # the guide appears once, not three times

# ragged lists and empties are fine
assert interleave([]) == [] and interleave([[], []]) == []
assert len(interleave([_cost, []])) == 2
```

``` python
# clustering: three copies and one original make two stories, and clusters are transitive
_wire = ('OpenAI said today that it is lowering prices for its newest model across all tiers, '
         'effective immediately for every API customer.')
_syn = [dict(href='https://a.invalid/x', title='OpenAI cuts prices', body=_wire),
        dict(href='https://b.invalid/y', title='OpenAI cuts prices', body=_wire),
        dict(href='https://c.invalid/z', title='OpenAI cuts prices', body=_wire),
        dict(href='https://openai.com/index/new-pricing', title='New pricing for our latest model',
             body='We are updating the per-token price of our newest model from today.')]
_cl = cluster_sources(_syn)
assert len(_cl) == 2, _cl                                  # three copies collapse, the original stands
assert _cl[0]['size'] == 3 and _cl[1]['size'] == 1
assert _cl[0]['canonical'] == 'https://a.invalid/x'        # named by its first (highest-ranked) member

_ind = independence(_syn)
assert _ind['n'] == 4 and _ind['sources'] == 2             # the number a reader actually needs
assert _ind['method'] == 'url+text' and _ind['confidence'] == 'medium'
assert _ind['limitations']                                 # always says what it cannot see

# transitivity: A~B and B~C is one family even where A and C alone fall short of the threshold
_chain = [dict(href='https://a.invalid/1', body='alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta'),
          dict(href='https://b.invalid/2', body='beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta iota'),
          dict(href='https://c.invalid/3', body='gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta iota kappa')]
assert jaccard(shingles(_chain[0]['body']), shingles(_chain[2]['body'])) < 0.6      # not a pair...
assert len(cluster_sources(_chain, threshold=0.5)) == 1, cluster_sources(_chain, 0.5)  # ...but one chain

# the same url twice is one source however differently it is described
assert len(cluster_sources([dict(href='https://x.com/a?utm_source=t', body='one two three four'),
                            dict(href='http://www.x.com/a', body='utterly different words here')])) == 1

# genuinely independent results stay independent
_div = [dict(href=f'https://s{i}.invalid/a', body=f'entirely separate subject number {i} here')
        for i in range(5)]
assert independence(_div)['sources'] == 5 and independence(_div)['score'] > independence(_syn)['score']

# no text to compare: degrade to url identity and say so rather than claiming confidence
_bare = [dict(href='https://a.invalid/1'), dict(href='https://b.invalid/2')]
assert independence(_bare)['method'] == 'url' and independence(_bare)['confidence'] == 'low'
assert any('too little text' in l for l in independence(_bare)['limitations'])
assert independence([]) == dict(n=0, sources=0, score=0.0, clusters=[], method='none',
                                confidence='low', limitations=[])

# and diversity carries the honest source count next to the url count
assert diversity(_syn)['n'] == 4 and diversity(_syn)['sources'] == 2
assert shingles('two words') == set() and jaccard(set(), {('a','b','c')}) == 0.0
```
